title: VOICELESS - From Thorns to Freedom
desc:
"The Voiceless series, debuting this June at the Mill Pond Gallery, was born directly from my own lived experiences and the internal struggles that have shaped my perspective. By intertwining detailed portraiture with botanical symbolism, I explore the invisible barriers we navigate within ourselves and the external barriers imposed on us by others. These paintings reflect a personal transition from silence to expression. 

 This exhibition is an invitation for others to witness that journey and perhaps recognize their own quiet resilience within the layers of colour and light." 

 Patricia Roncone is a professional artist based in Richmond Hill, specializing in watercolour on Aquabord, a medium that allows for luminous depth while freeing my work from reliance on traditional glass. Her upcoming solo exhibition at the Mill Pond Gallery this June marks a significant milestone, bridging technical application of medium with raw, emotional storytelling.    www.patriciaroncone.com 

 As well as the two images above, here are additional glimpses of her work. 

 

 

  

 Home to the Richmond Hill Group of Artists, our gallery features exhibitions that change regularly, showcasing the creativity of individual artists and small groups. You’ll find a wonderful variety of styles, mediums, and themes — there’s always something new to discover!

 Drop by often, meet the artists, and be inspired by the art and community that make the Mill Pond Gallery such a special place.

 Free parking and no admission fee

 All are welcome!

 Gallery Hours: 

 
 Saturdays and Sundays – 11 am to 5 pm

title: Parenting in the Digital Age
desc:
Audience: Adult

Managing children's social media and AI usage often feels like a constant battle over restrictions. Parents frequently find themselves caught between enforcing rules and maintaining a positive, healthy relationship with their children. In this talk, Kids Rights Canada will explore with you how to guide children and youth toward becoming responsible internet users. We will discuss common conflicts over screen time and demonstrate how these moments can be transformed into powerful educational opportunities. Parents will walk away with practical skills and the language needed to foster open dialogue, helping their children grow into resilient and responsible digital citizens.

title: PALS  drop in ( Pet Assisted Literacy Support) in the Library
desc:
Audience: All Ages, Children

Markham Public Library in partnership with One Health Partners, is thrilled to have PALS in the Library, an animal assisted reading program designed to motivate, inspire and support the development of literacy skills, social emotional learning and love of reading while also being neurodiversity and disability friendly. Young readers build confidence and capacity as they read out loud to a learning pal who is fun, furry and only requires reading to be punctuated with periodic pats. Friends would who just like to meet out furry friends and sit with them, are also welcome. This program will provide a unique, safe and fun learning opportunity for children to individually spend time with a certified therapy dog who is also temperament tested professionally evaluated, safety and health screened therapy dogs. In this drop in program, kids are invited (up to ) two at time to spend time with a certified therapy dog for 15 minutes.

title: Small Towns and Big Secrets: In Conversation with Bestselling Author Karin Slaughter
desc:
Join for a thrilling evening with acclaimed author Karin Slaughter as we chat about her North Falls series, consisting of We Are All Guilty Here, in which two teenage girls vanish in rural Georgia, and her upcoming sequel, The Secrets We Hide. In The Secrets We Hide, Slaughter welcomes readers back to North Falls. A small town with big secrets… 1601 Iris Drive looks like any other house on the quiet, residential street. 

 But rumors are rampant about the Vickery family, and what goes on behind closed doors. When gunshots ring out, Sheriff Emmy Clifton and her sister, ex-federal agent Jude Archer, discover a devastating crime scene. Allison Vickery has been murdered in her own kitchen, and her teenage daughter is bleeding upstairs, left for dead. Everyone thinks they know what happened. But secrets are buried everywhere in this small town. And it’s up to Emmy Clifton to uncover the truth.

desc:
Audience: Adult

🏷️What is your business brand? Whether you’re launching a new venture or navigating a season of growth, brand marketing is a vital component of your business. This session focuses on the practical fundamentals of brand marketing and why a consistent narrative is imperative at any stage of your journey. We’ll look at ways to uncover your own brand identity and how to effectively communicate your "why" in a crowded marketplace. We will have time for an audience Q&A to address your specific goals. Presenter's Bio: Candy Hon is a seasoned Marketing and Communications expert with in-depth experience in B2C marketing, sponsorship activations, and cross-functional team leadership. She’s adept at strengthening brand presence, driving engagement and meticulous campaign execution. Her previous portfolio includes several high-visibility brands such as WNBA, NBA Canada and Toronto Bike Share.

title: The Power of Connection: Creating Lasting Friendships in an Increasingly Lonely World with Dr. Marisa Franco
desc:
Join this virtual conversation with bestselling author Dr. Marisa Franco, one of the world’s leading experts in human connection. Her book, Platonic: How the Science of Attachment Can Help You Make–And Keep–Friends, explores the science of different attachment styles and how they impact our relationships often in ways we don’t realize. 

 In Platonic, Dr. Marisa G. Franco unpacks the latest, often counterintuitive findings about the bonds between us. For example, why your friends aren’t texting you back, and the myth of “friendships happening organically.” Dr. Franco explains that to make and keep friends, you must understand your attachment style—secure, anxious, or avoidant: it is the key to unlocking what’s working (and what’s failing) in your friendships. 

 Click HERE to register.

title: Migrant Heart: The Hidden Cost of the American Dream and Healing Through Storytelling with Reyna Grande
desc:
In her ambitious new memoir, Migrant Heart: Essays About Things I Can’t Forget, beloved bestselling author Reyna Grande illuminates the hidden cost of the American Dream and the complex journey of healing that follows survival.

 What is the true power of stories?
Can they heal the jagged edges of a traumatic childhood?
Is the cost of telling the story worth the price of the cure?

 With her signature blend of sophistication and raw honesty, Grande interrogates how living between two nations, two languages, and two identities has shaped the woman, mother, and writer she has become. 

 Moving from the legacy of violence in her hometown of Iguala, Mexico, to a bittersweet family vacation in Europe spent reconciling her own impoverished past with her children’s world of abundance, she uncovers startling truths about the nature of survival.

 Register today for this virtual talk if you identify as a seeker, a dreamer, or “anyone who believes in the enduring, transformative power of finding one’s voice.”

 Click HERE to register

title: Repair Cafe
desc:
Repair Cafés are free events that bring together those with broken items and those who can fix them.  

 York Region, in partnership with  NewMakeIt , offers a series of Repair Cafés across York Region, hosted at local libraries and community spaces. 

 From bicycle chains to bracelet clasps to torn pants, volunteer fixers are available to help repair your item free of charge, extending its life.   

 Each item repaired at a Repair Café is: 

 One less item wasted 
One less item purchased 
One more proud fixer 
One more smiling face 

 Since 2018, with the support of our community partners and volunteers, York Region Repair Cafés have fixed over 550 items.  
Please click HERE to book a time and find out which items may or may not be brought to be fixed.

This workshop will be led by award-winning author Deborah Kerbel, VPL’s first Writer-in-Residence. Deborah has published more than thirty books across genres, from picture books and graphic novels to young adult fiction. In May and June, she will offer writing workshops for all ages, along with one-on-one consultations, manuscript critiques, and drop-in Q&A sessions. To learn more, please visit www.vaughanpl.info/wir .
 
Deborah will cover the following points:
 
 Character
 What makes a good character? What do you need to know about your characters before you let them step foot onto your page? We will do a brainstorming writing exercise in character development. 
 Setting
 How different settings and scenes can shape your story and improve its readability. We will do an interactive exercise on setting selection. 
 Problem
 What’s going to give your story the narrative thrust? What problem will engage your reader right off the top and force dramatic reactions out of your characters? The central problem is what will make your reader CARE about your character and be compelled to turn the page to see how they resolve it. 
 Action
 Each word in your story has the task of pushing the narrative forward. But where does your story begin? And where does it end? Getting right to the heart of your story by identifying these points is essential. Once that’s done, a writer is free to jump right into the action. 
 
During the final part of the workshop, participants will write a scene using some of the character traits, setting ideas, and problems that were collectively brainstormed within the group.
 
Our teen programs are created to give teens their own space to connect and learn. For that reason, registration is limited to teens in grades 9–12. To explore library programs and events for children and adults, please see VPL's Library Program Guide .

desc:
ROQE LIVE 6 returns for an unforgettable evening of music, conversation, storytelling, and celebration.

 Hosted by Jian Ghomeshi.

 This sixth special edition of Roqe Live brings together an exceptional lineup of guests and performers, including

 
 legendary Iranian pop icon Shahram Shabpareh 
 psychologist and social media star Tina Parsa 
 beloved television personality Shally Zomorodi 
 adventurer and aviation hero Captain Christopher Behnam 
 singer-songwriter Darius Azar and his band 
 popular pianist Ghazal Piano 
 Roqe favourite Pegah Ganji 
 
 The evening will feature live performances, engaging interviews, memorable moments, and the presentation of the Roqe Media Icon Award to Shahram Shabpareh in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to Iranian music and culture over more than five decades.

 Whether you are a longtime supporter of Roqe or attending for the first time, this promises to be a unique live experience celebrating some of the most remarkable voices and personalities in the Iranian diaspora.

title: A Legal Guide to Estate Planning
desc:
Time: 7:00 PM

Feeling overwhelmed about the future? Learn the essentials of estate planning to protect your loved ones, secure your assets, and plan ahead with clarity and peace of mind. Please register on Eventbrite. Join in person or on Zoom. 
 
This presentation introduces participants to the essentials of estate planning. Participants will learn some basics about organizing their affairs, protecting their assets, and planning for incapacity through legal tools like wills and powers of attorney. 
 This session aims to make estate planning less intimidating and more understandable to help attendees gain confidence about the process. The presentation will be interactive, allowing participants to review their understanding of legal principles and ask questions. 
 
This program will be presented by Stefania Rotundu, a licensed estates lawyer at Arhire Law. Stefania obtained her law degree from the University of Ottawa and holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Toronto. She is currently enrolled in the Society of Trust and Estate Practitioners program for lawyers.

title: Books & Biscotti
desc:
Time: 6:00 PM

Celebrate Italian Heritage Month with readings from local authors. Free biscotti and coffee will be provided. Event organized in partnership with the Association of Italian Canadian Writers. 
 
Books & Biscotti will also include a mercato: nineteen authors, all members of the AICW, will have tables set up throughout the lobby where they will be able to promote and sell copies of their books.
 
 Featured Speakers: 
 
 Rosanna Micelotta Battigelli is an award-winning author in several genres. Rosanna was born in Calabria and immigrated to Canada with her family at three years of age. Along with her award-winning books La Brigantessa and Pigeon Soup & Other Stories, Rosanna has had six romance novels published with Harlequin/Mills & Boon (Harper Collins) and two children’s books published with Pajama Press. Her latest publications are Product of Italy, Made in Canada: An Immigrant’s Love Letter to Food, Family, and Resilience (Latitude 46 Publishing) and Co-Editor of Mum’s The Word, Unique stories that will surprise you (Guernica Editions). Rosanna lives in Sudbury, Ontario.
 
 John Calabro was born in Sicily and grew up in France. He has been an educator, publisher, cultural entrepreneur, and published author. Bellecour, published in 2005 by Guernica Editions, was named by the Globe and Mail as one of the top 5 First Fiction in 2005. The Cousin came out in 2009 with Quattro Books. Its French translation, Le Cousin, published by Lévesque Editeur in 2012, was shortlisted for a GG in Canada. An Imperfect Man was published by Quattro Books in 2012. Laura’s Uncovering was published in 2024 by Ekstasis Editions. Bellecour was reprinted by Raspa Editions in 2025.
 
 Domenico Capilongo’s work has appeared in several national and international literary magazines. His first book of poetry, I thought elvis was Italian, was short-listed for the 2010 F.G. Bressani Literary Prize, and his hold the note collection was long-listed for the 2011 ReLit Award. His latest book of poems, 1972, won 3rd Place in the 2024 Pier Di Cicco Poetry Award, and in 2024 he won the Premio Italia Radici Nel Mondo International Literary Competition for his short story "Semi" ("Seeds").
 
 Caterina Nella Cotrupi is an Italian-born Canadian writer, translator, and literary critic. She holds a degree in law and a PhD in Comparative Literature from the University of Toronto. Nella has worked as a lawyer and as a professor of literature and law. Her publications include Northrop Frye and the Poetics of Process, and the forthcoming bilingual collection, LA POESIA DI CAROL SHIELDS. Nella has published numerous essays, poems, and short stories and was a finalist for the Winston Collins/Descant Prize for poetry.
 
 Rosina Fazzolari is currently working on her debut novel. She presented her work at the Conference of the Association of Italian-Canadian Writers in September of 2024, and at the Accenti Conference in P.E.I in June of 2025. One of her short stories was published in Accenti Magazine in November of 2025. As a second-generation daughter of Italian immigrants, Rosina’s storytelling currently focuses on the Italian-Canadian immigrant experience, including reverse immigration.
 
 Elio Iannaci is an award-winning writer, interdisciplinary scholar, poet, and arts reporter for The Globe and Mail. He has contributed to more than 80 publications worldwide, including Vogue Italia, The Hollywood Reporter, Maclean’s, The Toronto Star, and IN magazine. His Master’s thesis, Queer-Diva Collaboration in 20th Century Popular Music, was nominated for a Governor General’s Gold Medal. Some of his most notable profiles include Sophia Loren, Barbra Streisand, Lady Gaga, Joni Mitchell, and Beyoncé. In 2017, The Writer's Trust of Canada asked Iannacci to be a juror for the Dayne Ogilvie Prize, a literary award dedicated to emerging LGBTQ2IA+ authors. His literary own work can be found in books such as Here and Now: An Anthology of Queer Italian-Canadian Writing Volumes 1 & 2, Dolly on Dolly: Interviews & Encounters, and an upcoming anthology of Italian-Canadian writing titled The Nuances of Love. 
 
 Darlene Madott has written ten books, including Winners and Losers (2023), and her forthcoming book, Closing Ceremonies, includes a story short-listed in the inaugural Nona Heaslip “Best Canadian Short Fiction.” She has been shortlisted for the Carter V. Cooper Short Fiction Award three times, as well as being a frequent finalist for Accenti Magazine competitions, among others.

His Master’s thesis, Queer-Diva Collaboration in 20th Century Popular Music, was nominated for a Governor General’s Gold Medal. Some of his most notable profiles include Sophia Loren, Barbra Streisand, Lady Gaga, Joni Mitchell, and Beyoncé. In 2017, The Writer's Trust of Canada asked Iannacci to be a juror for the Dayne Ogilvie Prize, a literary award dedicated to emerging LGBTQ2IA+ authors. His literary own work can be found in books such as Here and Now: An Anthology of Queer Italian-Canadian Writing Volumes 1 & 2, Dolly on Dolly: Interviews & Encounters, and an upcoming anthology of Italian-Canadian writing titled The Nuances of Love. Darlene Madott has written ten books, including Winners and Losers (2023), and her forthcoming book, Closing Ceremonies, includes a story short-listed in the inaugural Nona Heaslip “Best Canadian Short Fiction.” She has been shortlisted for the Carter V. Cooper Short Fiction Award three times, as well as being a frequent finalist for Accenti Magazine competitions, among others.

title: De-stressing The Downsizing Process
desc:
Time: 2:00 PM

This session will provide an overview of the downsizing process and provide a practical plan on how to get ready for your big move. 
 
If you’re thinking about moving to a smaller home or have already made the decision, the downsizing process can be a daunting one, leaving you wondering where to start. 
 
You’ve likely accumulated many items and memories along the way, especially if you’ve lived in your home for several decades. Moving from a larger space to a smaller one means making lots of decisions ahead of time: How do you decide what to keep and let go of? How can you determine if your current furniture will fit in your new space? What do you do with the items that are no longer needed?
 
Presented by The Organizing Doula.

title: Living Well Fair
desc:
Time: 10:00 AM

Celebrate Seniors Month by discovering ways to live your best life. This event will feature community and wellness tables, workshops, and creative activities to help you connect and learn. 
 Please note that some sessions require registration. Please register on Eventbrite or by calling the library at 905-653-7323.
 For all registered sessions, walk-ins may be admitted on a first-come, first-served basis on the day of the event if space allows. 
 
 Registered sessions: 
 
 10:00 am – 11:00 am: Sound Bath with Project Healing (in the upstairs program room) 


A sound bath is a meditative form of sonic therapy. They help in maintaining a sense of well-being and support the enhancement of our mental, emotional, and physical health. This session is presented by Project Healing .
 
 11:00 am – 11:45 am: Navigating Health Misinformation with McMaster University (in the Teen Room) 


This session will explore the risks of health misinformation and will provide strategies for identifying reliable sources and how to effectively search for evidence-based health information. Presented by a McMaster University librarian. 
 
 12:00 pm – 12:45 pm: Human Connection 101: Building the Foundation for a Happy & Health Life with Genwell (in the Teen Room) 


We will explore how fostering human connections can dramatically improve your well-being and discover practical strategies for building meaningful relationships that enrich your life. This session is presented by GenWell . 
 
 1:00 pm – 1:45 pm: Creative Age: Mindful Gardening Terrarium Workshop with Cortellucci Hospice Vaughan (in the upstairs program room) 


This program offers a fun, hands-on way to relax, get creative, and connect with nature. Participants are guided through the process of designing and creating their own mini indoor garden using soil, plants, and decorative touches. This program is facilitated by a Recreation Therapist from Cortellucci Hospice Vaughan .
 
 Community Partner Tables:

York Farm Fresh

title: Artists in Residence - Mill Pond Gallery, with Dalia Manoim.
desc:
Each Tuesday throughout July and August, members of the Richmond Hill Group of Artists will begin a one week residency in the Mill Pond Gallery.  
Would you like to see how artists create their work? Drop in often to see the works in progress, talk to our artists and enjoy the work on display at the gallery.

 This week you will see complete work and work in progress from Dalia Manoim.

 A collection of mixed-media paintings where wildflowers and poppies spill from seashells, and the garden meets the sea. Each piece is built up in rich texture, color, and light – like treasures the tide carried in and left blooming on the shore. An invitation to slow down and look closely at the small, luminous worlds where land and water meet.

 In my art the extraordinary meets the everyday through the lens of endless possibilities. Whether through vibrant colors or intricate textures, my art evokes emotions and sparks conversations about the beauty of life and the courage to embrace our true selves.
Each artwork tells a story, encouraging contemplation and inspiring a sense of freedom and transformation. I believe in the power to Inspire Through Art, creating experiences that encourage self-discovery and reflection – Dalia  

 Many Thursday evenings the City of Richmond Hill hosts “Concerts in The Park” at the Mill Pond Park.  The gallery will be open until after the concert.  Stop by for a visit!

There is never an admission fee and all are welcome!

title: Matinée francophone  : L’histoire des Hurons-Wendats avec Dominic Ste-Marie
desc:
Categories: Adult Programs

Matinée francophone:
The History of the Huron-Wendat with Dominic Ste-Marie

Matinée Francophone

Discover the history of the Wendat people in southern Ontario and learn about their present-day community in Wendake, Québec. Join Dominic Ste-Marie for an engaging presentation exploring the rich history, living culture, and enduring legacy of the Wendat Nation through storytelling and conversation.

Following the presentation, participants are invited to enjoy coffee and fresh croissants while continuing the discussion in a relaxed and welcoming setting.

About the Speaker

Dominic Ste-Marie is a proud member of the Wendat Nation and the Yanariskwa (Wolf) Clan.

An accomplished storyteller, interpretive guide, lecturer, and voice narrator, Dominic is passionate about sharing Wendat culture through traditional stories, legends, and mythology. Based in Wendake, Québec, he combines his knowledge of history, politics, and economics with the art of storytelling to help audiences discover the richness of Wendat cultural heritage and identity.

Date Saturday, July 18
Time 10:30 am — 12:30 pm
Location Founders' Lounge

Free with admission. Registration required.

Book Tickets

Led by Innu artist and designer Raphaëlle Langevin, this hands-on workshop will invite children to create their own bracelet inspired by traditional First Nations breastplates.

Raphaëlle Langevin is an Indigenous fashion designer, a member of the Pekuakamiulnuatsh community of Mashteuiatsh, and a mother of two. Creative and ambitious, she founded Matsheshu Créations to provide a platform for First Nations craftswomen and contribute to the economic development of her community. title: Money Smarts for Grades 7 & 8 (Budgeting & Expenses)
desc:
Audience: Children

What is budgeting and expenses? This engaging program helps gr 7 & 8 students build real‑world money skills by exploring budgeting, earning income, saving, and setting meaningful goals. They learn how to make thoughtful choices between needs and wants, understand how their skills connect to future earning potential, and discover why saving—even in small amounts—can create big results over time. The session also introduces S.M.A.R.T. goal setting to help students turn their dreams into achievable plans. Presenter's bio: This workshop is facilitated by Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada (CPA Canada). CPA Canada is one of the largest national accounting organizations globally, representing over 220,000 members. It promotes transparency in financial markets, prepares members for a changing business environment, and contributes to standard setting and public policy. It also collaborates with international bodies to strengthen the global accounting profession. For more information, visit www.cpacanada.ca

desc:
Enjoy a relaxing evening of walking the trails and listening for native frogs at this time of year.

 Learn about Ontario’s frogs and toads and how to identify them by their unique calls. We’ll also show you how you can get involved with citizen science programs to monitor amphibian populations across Ontario.

 This event is intended for Ages 6+:

 
 Beginner level information 
 Activities and concepts that are friendly for all ages 
 Intended audience includes children, youth, and adults 
 Trail difficulty (10 being the most difficult): 6/10 
 
 Price : Free. Registration is required and is limited. Click HERE to register.

 Please DO NOT park in the Bond Lake parking lot. Please park in the parking lot with the Movati Gym & Farm Boy. We will meet on the sidewalk on the south west corner of the intersection (Silver Maple Rd. & Yonge St.).

 The Oak Ridges Corridor Conservation Reserve (ORCCR) is a 175-plus hectare property located in Richmond Hill. It is home to forests, wetlands, meadows, kettle lakes, and parts of the the Humber River. 

 These ORCCR events are part of a series of hikes to encourage Richmond Hill residents to get out in their community and learn more about the rich history and importance of the Humber River.

title: Community Action Grant Office Hour/Drop-in
desc:
Audience: Adult, Youth

United Way Greater Toronto is now accepting applications for the 2026–2027 South Markham Community Action Grants. Funding is available for resident-led and agency or collaborative projects that support community-identified neighbourhood priorities, with grants ranging from $5,000 to $100,000. Applications are open from May 25 to September 11, 2026. Drop-in office hours will be hosted at the Aaniin Community Centre from 3 - 5 pm on July 9 and at the Milliken Mills Public Library from 5 - 7 pm on August 4. Residents are also invited to register for grant writing training session that will be hosted on July 9 at Aaniin Community Centre at 5:30 - 7 pm (register here: https://forms.office.com/r/ckeJ7SPpXA ). Learn more at https://uwgt.org/south-markham. South Markham Community Action Table bio: South Markham Connects is led by ACSA, a non-profit, multi-service agency dedicated to addressing community needs and empowering children, youth, newcomers, and underserved communities to build a better tomorrow. Working across York Region, ACSA leads community-driven initiatives in South Markham, including the South Markham Community Action Table (SMCAT), the Neighbourhood Solutions Strategy (NSS), and the Traumatic Incident Response Protocol (TIRP). Learn more at https://uwgt.org/south-markham.

There is never an admission fee and all are welcome!

title: Wagging Tails, Happy Hearts: An Introduction to Responsible Dog Ownership
desc:
Audience: All Ages, Children

Join us for an educational presentation where we will explore the wonderful world of responsible dog ownership! Wagging Tails, Happy Hearts aims to teach families essential skills and knowledge needed to care for our furry friends. Whether you're thinking about getting a dog, recently adopted one, or have been a dog owner for years, this seminar is the perfect place to enhance your knowledge. Led by Valerie from SSH Canine Academy , a canine behavior specialist with a passion for creating lasting connections between dogs and their families, this presentation will empower you with the tools to be a confident and compassionate dog owner. In this program, you’ll discover the joys of having a dog while learning about the responsibilities that come with pet ownership. Valerie will guide you through essential topics such as costs, regular exercise, dog training, and maintaining your pup’s health and happiness. Joining Valerie will be her trusted dog Bluey! Bluey will help demonstrate key lessons, such as how to safely interact with dogs, understand their body language, and respect their space. During the presentation, kids will have a chance to meet Bluey and see these skills in a fun and engaging way, fostering positive and fulfilling relationships with dogs. By the end of the presentation, families will be well-equipped with the knowledge and skills to become responsible and loving dog owners. Let’s take this exciting journey together with Valerie’s expert guidance and Bluey’s adorable assistance to create a harmonious bond between families and their canine pals! Learn more about SSH Canine Academy! Website: www.sshcanineacademy.com Instagram: @ssh.canineacademy & @valthedogpal Tiktok: @valthedogpal Youtube: @valthedogpal

title: 10 Health Financial Management Habits
desc:
Audience: Adult, Older Adult

Take Charge of Your Financial Fitness! This 60‑minute session helps participants become more confident and effective money managers by exploring the essentials of financial literacy. Attendees will assess their own financial fitness, learn the Ten Healthy Habits of Financial Management, and understand how goal‑setting and values shape smart financial decisions. The program also highlights common financial challenges, practical strategies for getting your financial house in order, and the social issues tied to money management. Participants leave with useful tools—including budgeting, goal‑setting, and self‑assessment resources—to support healthier financial habits. Presenter's bio: This workshop is facilitated by Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada (CPA Canada). CPA Canada is one of the largest national accounting organizations globally, representing over 220,000 members. It promotes transparency in financial markets, prepares members for a changing business environment, and contributes to standard setting and public policy. It also collaborates with international bodies to strengthen the global accounting profession. For more information, visit www.cpacanada.ca

title: Yawatsira’ Sunday
desc:
Categories: Family Programs

Yawatsira’ Sunday

Bilingual Family Sunday

With ceremonies, storytelling and artmaking, the McMichael join us for a bilingual celebration of  Indigenous culture and creativity, as well as the Indigenous presence along the shores of Humber River.

Book Tickets

Vaughan Public Library Toddler Storytelling

French

Join us for a French storytime! The best way to learn and practice French, having fun with wonderful stories and songs led by Vaughan Public Library. We will read J’ai le coeur rempli de bonheur, by Monique Gray Smith.

Toddler Storytelling
Time 10:30 AM — 11 AM
Ages 2 — 5
Location Founders' Lounge

Indigenous Ceremony with Elder Shelley Charles

English

Please join us in front of the gallery for a ceremonial circle and knowledge sharing with Elder Shelley Charles from Chippewas of Georgina Island.

Outdoor Demonstration
Time 11 AM
Ages All ages
Location Courtyard

Bilingual Bracelet-Making Workshop

English & French

Led by Innu artist and designer Raphaëlle Langevin, this hands-on workshop will invite children to create their own bracelet inspired by traditional First Nations breastplates.

About the artist

Raphaëlle Langevin is an Indigenous fashion designer, a member of the Pekuakamiulnuatsh community of Mashteuiatsh, and a mother of two. Creative and ambitious, she founded Matsheshu Créations to provide a platform for First Nations craftswomen and contribute to the economic development of her community. Through her handcrafted jewelry collections, beading kits, and clothing, Raphaëlle shares First Nations ancestral techniques and knowledge with the next generation.

Workshop
Time 11:30 AM — 3 PM
Ages 4 — 12
Location Grand Hall

Storytelling Circle—Storytellers & Imagemakers

English & French

Through the guided viewing of selected artworks created by Indigenous artists, learn what role art played in their traditional culture and discover how different is this approach today.

Storytelling Circle
English 11:30 AM & 2 PM
French 12:30 PM
Ages 6 — 12
Location Grand Hall

Huron-Wendat Creation Story—Performance by Dominic Ste-Marie

English & French

Discover Huron-Wendat culture and identity through an engaging storytelling performance by Dominic Ste-Marie, a Wendat storyteller and cultural educator. Dominic will share a traditional Creation Story and invite audiences into a conversation about the meaning, origins, and ongoing importance of legends within Wendat culture.

About the Artist

Dominic Ste-Marie is a proud member of the Wendat Nation from the Yanariskwa (Wolf) clan. A skilled storyteller, guide interpreter, speaker, and voice narrator, Dominic passionately shares his culture through traditional Wendat legends and mythology.

Performance
English 1:30 — 2:15 PM
French 2:30 — 3 PM
Ages All ages
Location Gallery 8

Photo & Video Release

Please be advised that staff from the McMichael may be capturing photos and video footage during our special events. These images may be used, repurposed, and published across various platforms, including news articles, social media channels, and our website. Additionally, these images may be shared with our event partners/sponsors.

title: Beyond Prenatals: Preparing Your Body for Pregnancy
desc:
Audience: Adult

Thinking of trying for a baby in the next few months or years, but not sure where to start? Many people are told to “just start trying,” yet receive little guidance on what that actually looks like or how to support their health beforehand. Add in all the information online, and it can quickly feel confusing and overwhelming. Join naturopathic doctor Dr. Beatrice Hai for an educational webinar on preconception health and the foundations of fertility. This session will help you understand what actually supports reproductive health in the months leading up to conception, including cycle awareness and ovulation, key lifestyle and nutritional foundations, common factors that can influence fertility, and simple, practical steps to support your body before trying to conceive. Designed for anyone planning ahead or hoping to feel more informed and empowered in their fertility journey.

title: Thriving in Transition - Helping Teens Prepare Socially and Emotionally for High School
desc:
Audience: Adult, Youth

This workshop is designed for teens aged 3-14 who are preparing for the social, academic, and emotional changes that come with moving into a new school or starting high school. Participants explore their worries and anticipations around major life transitions, build practical strategies for managing routines and stress, and strengthen coping skills, confidence, and emotional awareness. Through interactive reflection activities, small-group discussions, and facilitator-led conversations, teens practice navigating new environments, balancing responsibilities, and preparing for academic, social, and lifestyle changes. The session provides a supportive space to share experiences, problem-solve, and feel more confident and grounded as they step into the next stage of school and life. Please note- this is a highly interaction based session and would need video and audio participation from teens. Please attend from a private space where you feel comfortable to unmute and share.

title: Commemoration of Emancipation Day
desc:
Emancipation Day commemorates the abolition of slavery across the British Empire in 1834, and provides an opportunity to reflect on our shared history while recognizing the enduring legacy, resilience, and contributions of Black Canadians.

 Join Richmond Hill Public Library and the York Region Alliance of African Canadian Communities (YRAACC) for a community commemoration featuring music and remarks as we honour this important day and reaffirm our collective commitment to equity, inclusion, and justice.

 The event is happening in the Cafe Space - First Floor.
